findings.claim: The About page says 'USGS says its map services are free and in the public domain' about imagery that has roads and names, with no exception. The branch's own research refutes an unqualified public-domain claim for ImageryTopo roads.
findings.evidence: research/globe/validation-evidence/labels-on-globe.json review.refuted_claims[6]: 'USGS public domain unqualified for ImageryTopo roads: FAQ names US Topo exceptions'; facts[1]: public domain 'except for' three US Topo cases, including 2010-2016 road data that is commercially licensed. The live service description (fetched 2026-10-18, imagery-work/review-probe/svc.json) says ImageryTopo is orthoimagery and US Topo vector data. imagery-switch-verification.json owner_decisions[0] leaves the road licence open. tests/test_site.py:1251 and :1307 assert 'public domain' and would need the same change.
findings.fix: Qualify the sentence: 'USGS says its map services are free and in the public domain, except some US Topo road data; USGS has not stated a licence for this service's road and name layers.' Keep the owner decision open in D32 and update tests/test_site.py:1251 and :1307 to match.

findings.claim: The imagery timing text, rendered on the public About page, says 'A service, not dated; USGS says when each area was flown on its own site'. USGS's own service metadata gives a refresh date, and no record supports the flight-date claim.
findings.evidence: Live service metadata (2026-10-18, imagery-work/review-probe/svc.json): copyrightText 'USGS The National Map: Orthoimagery and US Topo. Data refreshed April, 2026.v1.2.'; the description says NAIP is the majority of the imagery source and 'The data is 1-meter pixel resolution with leaf-on'. A search of research/globe/validation-evidence for flown, acquisition and capture date finds no USGS statement of per-area flight dates. tests/test_site.py:1318 locks 'not dated' in.
findings.fix: Replace with a checked statement, for example: 'The tiles carry no date. USGS's service says its data were refreshed in April 2026; its main source is leaf-on NAIP imagery. Flight dates are not shown here.' Update tests/test_site.py:1318 to match, and verify any flight-date claim before publishing it.

findings.claim: D32's Why says 'Of the imagery sources checked, USGS is the only one that is public domain'. The record shows other public-domain sources: NAIP (the service's main source), Montana State Library content, and NASA-led data under CC0.
findings.evidence: research/globe/validation-evidence/montana-imagery-buildings.json terms[1]: NAIP 'Media Sources/Usage: Public Domain' (USGS); the live service description names NAIP as the majority source; terms[0]: Montana State Library content is public domain, and urls_checked[3] lists its 1955/1964/1972 MapServers. gibs.json license: NASA-led mission data 'licensed as Creative Commons Zero (CC0)' under NASA guidance; GIBS itself is 'acknowledgment, not a licence', and base-imagery.json facts[14] records a 'not in the public domain' statement, so the status is contested. The sentence reads as three tests together, so the conjunctive reading saves part of it, but the text does not say so.
findings.fix: State the tests one by one, for example: 'USGS's service is public domain by USGS's statement (with the US Topo exceptions), needs no key, and serves zoom 16. Its main imagery is NAIP, which USGS also lists as public domain. NASA GIBS is CC0 for NASA-led data, but its levels stop at 8 and it has no roads or names. Esri and EOX are barred or non-commercial.'

findings.fix: Replace the text in sources.py and DESIGN.md with what happens: 'A tile that does not load leaves a plain background with the Montana outline, state lines and town bubbles; roads, lakes, counties and place names stay hidden until a tile loads.' Putting the white vector base back under the tiles would draw names under the photo, which the brief rules out. Then settle the owner decision on a failure line, since the credit still shows with no imagery.

findings.claim: D32's Why says: 'The white map stays the default because it is the look Carson asked for in D28.'
findings.evidence: D28 (lines 359-362) records Carson asking for a map that 'looks like' Apple Weather's precipitation map. It never asks for a white map, and D28's basemap was the team's own choice ('our own vector map', around line 380). The owner's actual decision is the 2026-10-17 one in the brief: keep the existing white vector base map as the default after comparing the Google satellite view.
findings.fix: Cite Carson's 2026-10-17 decision as the reason for the white default and drop the D28 attribution.

findings.claim: Observations say that on a short landscape phone the credit row is 'hidden until the info button opens the legend'.
findings.evidence: At 667x375, 740x360 and 844x390 with imagery on, the credit row starts at y=363, below the visible legend. The info button (#legend-info, map.js 1518-1523) only toggles the legend note, not the keys. The legend column scrolls (overflow auto, 213 px visible of 291 px), and after scrolling the credit sits at y=285-313 in a 375 px viewport (imagery-work/review/verify_landscape.py, verify_info.py, verify_scroll.py). So the credit is reachable by scrolling, and the note is wrong. The smoke check reads DOM text, so it cannot see this.
findings.fix: Correct the observation. Optionally keep the credit in view on short landscape (for example beside the Map data link), and have the smoke test check that the credit is inside the viewport at 667x375.

findings.claim: 'Calgary, Lethbridge, Regina and Toronto get a blank white tile of about 2.4 to 2.8 KB' at zoom 9.
findings.evidence: Calgary, Lethbridge and Regina at z9: 2,419 bytes, mean 255.0, std 0 (blank). Toronto at z9: 2,767 bytes, mean 254.7, std 6.0 (near-white with faint marks). Measured by the reviewer from the live host (imagery-work/review/tiles_check.json; probe-nonus.json). Toronto was checked only by byte size in the team's probe.
findings.fix: Say 'a blank or near-white tile' for Toronto, or measure it and state the result.

findings.claim: 'Of the imagery sources checked, USGS is the only one that is public domain, needs no key and serves tiles to a browser at zoom 16.' This is a superlative about a provider, which AGENTS.md rule 9 discourages.
findings.evidence: rights-matrix.json lists NASA GIBS as CC0 with no key. base-imagery.json terms_by_source says GIBS has 'No licence text on GIBS pages; guideline scope ambiguous'. No record gives a GIBS zoom limit, so the zoom-16 leg of the comparison has no recorded basis. The research conflicts on GIBS's licence.
findings.fix: State only what was checked: 'Of the sources in base-imagery.json, only USGS states a public-domain licence and serves tiles at zoom 16; GIBS's licence text is not stated and its zoom limit was not checked.'

findings.claim: The imagery timing text says 'USGS says when each area was flown on its own site'. The text is printed on the About page through the sources table.
findings.evidence: No file in research/globe/validation-evidence records this USGS statement or any acquisition-date source for ImageryTopo. A search for 'flown', 'acquisition' and 'capture date' finds nothing relevant.
findings.fix: Verify the statement on a live USGS page and cite it in the evidence file, or drop the clause.

findings.claim: The About page says 'USGS says its map services are free and in the public domain' with no qualifier. DECISIONS line 543 also gives the credit as 'USDA, USGS, The National Map'.
findings.evidence: The FAQ statement is blanket, with US Topo exceptions, and the record says 'Current ImageryTopo road licence not stated' (labels-on-globe.json; rights-matrix row 'ImageryTopo road licence unverified'). USGS's own imagery credit in the record is 'USDA, USGS' (base-imagery.json terms). 'USDA, USGS, The National Map' is the product's longer form, not USGS's stated credit.
findings.fix: About: 'USGS's FAQ says its map services are free and in the public domain; USGS does not state a licence for the road and name layers of this service.' DECISIONS: say the product credit adds the service name to USGS's 'USDA, USGS'.

findings.claim: The existing test named test_map_page_loads_only_files_from_this_site still carries the old rule's name, and the research files point to it as the site-files rule.
findings.evidence: The test checks only the default map page's script, link and img tags. AGENTS.md rule 4 now allows the imagery tiles, which this test does not mention. The name overstates the rule.
findings.fix: Rename it (for example test_map_page_tags_load_only_site_files) and add a comment that the imagery tiles are the one exception (D32).

findings.claim: D28 says 'Nothing from third-party servers but data:'. D32's rule-change bullet (line 547) does not say that it amends this D28 line.
findings.evidence: The D28 line is still unqualified, and D32 amends it for the Map page.
findings.fix: Add 'This amends the D28 line about third-party servers' to D32's rule-change bullet.

findings.claim: A page opened with ?base=imagery starts on imagery and fetches tiles at once, with no switch. The privacy sentence is shown only inside the Layers menu and on About, so a shared link can send the viewer's IP to USGS with no visible notice.
findings.evidence: imagery-work/review/verify-default.json G_open_direct: 35 host requests on arrival, no click. Brief item 2 asks for this URL behaviour, but the brief's opening paragraph says tiles stream 'only after the viewer switches to it'. The two conflict.
findings.fix: Owner decision: keep the URL opt-in, or show the one-line privacy note on arrival whenever the URL opens Imagery.

findings.claim: On a 667x375 landscape phone the Imagery choice sits below the bottom of the Layers menu on first view.
findings.evidence: The menu is 55 to 362 px tall and scrolls (max-height 307 px). The Imagery label spans 310 to 387 px (402 px when Imagery is on). It is reachable by scrolling and by Tab and arrow keys (verified), but not visible on first open.
findings.fix: Accept and note it, or move the Base map group above the weather layers on short screens.

findings.claim: The brief asks for screenshots at 1280x800 and 390x844 in both modes 'for the record'.
findings.evidence: The record's screenshot paths point at scratch folders outside the repo, and the record says the PNG files are not in the repo.
findings.fix: Keep a small set of desktop and phone PNGs in both modes with the evidence record, or state plainly that the record has none.

fix.tests: Unit tests: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests, Ran 378 tests, OK on the final edits (the base commit had 363). Browser, final flag-on sample build with --storm-layers: PW_CHROMIUM=/opt/pw-browsers/chromium python3 tools/smoke_map.py <build> --shots <dir> PASS (exit 0), no Note lines, so the tile answered and drew. tools/smoke_pages.py on the same build: PASS at 288, 320, 375, 768 and 1440 px, light and dark. Mutants, on copies of the flag-on build: (a) leftover tile layer (removeLayer deleted from setBase) passed the smoke test before the fix (exit 0) and fails after it (exit 1, leftover-layer messages on the first and second switch back). (b) base-map shapes and names not hidden (CSS rule removed): check_imagery_refused fails with 46 shapes and 38 names drawn with no tiles. Full runs of the final flag-on build: 6 of 7 passed; the one timeout was in the existing check_empty_layer_switch (see open_issues). Full runs of the final default build: 3 of 5 passed; two timed out, one of them in check_empty_layer_switch, and the other was the formal direct run whose check was not logged. Interleaved base versus final, flag on, same load window: base pairs 1 to 4 all passed; final pairs 1 to 3 all passed; final pair 4 and pair 5 were still running when this report was made.
failures: Formal smoke run of the final default build timed out (Page.goto, 30 s) in an existing check. A second run of the same build timed out in check_empty_layer_switch. The timeouts are a pre-existing race, not an imagery failure, but the default smoke step is not reliably green on this loaded machine.

The review record is not written yet. imagery-switch-review.json does not exist, and imagery-switch-verification.json still has the uncorrected observations (the Canadian tiles, the tile sizes, and the landscape credit claim). The scripts are ready at imagery-work/fix/scripts/update_evidence.py (run once) and imagery-work/fix/scripts/write_review.py (run after the formal default run). Neither has been run.
The formal smoke run on the final default build has not been recorded as a clean pass. The earlier direct run timed out.
The interleaved base-versus-final comparison is incomplete (final pair 4 and pair 5 pending at report time). The results so far are all PASS.
open_issues: Owner: the road and name licence for ImageryTopo. USGS states none. The US Topo exception covers commercially licensed road data in most 2010 to 2016 maps, so this is not a clearance.
Owner: a link that starts on Imagery (?base=imagery) loads tiles as the page opens, and the privacy line sits inside the closed Layers menu. Show the line on arrival, or change the link behaviour?
Owner: on-screen credit wording. It omits US Topo and does not use the acknowledgment USGS requests: 'Map services and data available from U.S. Geological Survey, National Geospatial Program.'
Owner: whether a failed tile should show words. Today a plain near-white background shows and the credit row still shows.
Owner: the privacy line could also say that tile requests carry the page address and the browser User-Agent. D32 records both.
Owner: on a 667x375 phone the Imagery choice needs a scroll of the Layers menu on first view. Accept it, or move the Base map group up on short screens.

Pre-existing, not changed in this stage: check_empty_layer_switch holds the precipitation pictures and then waits for the load event with page.goto, so its page load can time out under CPU load. The check was not edited in this stage, and the same check exists at the base commit. A timeout under load was reproduced on the base build (1 of 5 runs). The smallest fix is wait_until='domcontentloaded' in that check, since the check already waits for the is-loading class. This needs a parent or owner decision because it affects the branch's Website smoke step.
The smoke wrapper reports 'a check could not run: Page.goto: Timeout' without naming the check, which slowed triage here. Naming the check is a small follow-up; not changed.
fix.notes:
Stage D result: 28 review findings were checked. 1 blocking and 6 major findings were reproduced or checked against live sources. All are fixed or recorded, with these exceptions. F5 and F26 keep the link behaviour the brief asks for; only the wording was corrected. F6 and F12 are recorded or partly fixed; the wording stays an owner decision. F27 is recorded as open. F28 is stated plainly, since the PNGs are not committed.

Fixes: (1) Blocking F16, the leftover tile layer after switching back. tools/smoke_map.py now asserts after each switch back that the layer and its pictures are gone, and again after a second round. (2) F17, a failed tile. The brief's 'white map showing underneath' was wrong: with every tile refused the map is a near-white field with the outline, state lines and town bubbles, and the base map's shapes and names are hidden. sources.py, DESIGN.md and D32 now say that, and a new check_imagery_refused in smoke_map.py locks it. (3) F1 to F3 and F21: the public-domain claim is qualified (US Topo exceptions, no stated licence for ImageryTopo roads and names). The 'flown on its own site' claim is removed; the live service gives a refresh date of April 2026 and says the main source is leaf-on NAIP. D32's uniqueness claim is replaced by the tests each source meets in the record. (4) F4 and F18: D32 no longer credits D28 for the white default; it cites Carson's 2026-10-17 decision, and the reason is not recorded. (5) Minor fixes: the test names (card, site-files), the zoom and Canada wording, the 15.7 to 35.7 KB tile sizes, the Esri and GIBS wording, the D-G15 citation, the Blue Marble units text, the stale DESIGN.md basemap line, the D27 amendment note, and the comment about where the host name lives.

Corrections to the reviewer's citations: the 'USDA, USGS' credit is the record's USGS credit, and the on-screen credit adds the service name. The 'D28 line 344' text is in D27. The US Topo exception is on the USGS costs FAQ, not the terms FAQ. The reviewer's 'satellite photographs' units wording was not used, because the flag-off build must not name the satellite picture, and the test that enforces it caught the first try.

Git: nothing committed, pushed or staged. The 12 tracked files are modified, and imagery-switch-verification.json is untracked.

To finish, in order: (a) run python3 -I imagery-work/fix/scripts/update_evidence.py once (it asserts and will not run twice); (b) run PW_CHROMIUM=/opt/pw-browsers/chromium python3 tools/smoke_map.py imagery-work/fix/final-default > imagery-work/fix/log-smoke-final-default-formal.txt 2>&1 (all paths under the scratchpad directory); (c) run python3 -I imagery-work/fix/scripts/write_review.py, which writes research/globe/validation-evidence/imagery-switch-review.json from the logs; (d) read the interleaved log imagery-work/fix/log-interleaved.txt for pairs 4 and 5. All scratch probes and logs are under imagery-work/fix/ and are not in the repo.
